content: This information does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or suitable for you. It is not intended to replace individual medical advice and should not substitute for the guidance of your healthcare professional. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Uses: This medication is prescribed to treat various fungal infections. It is also used to prevent fungal infections in patients undergoing stem cell transplants. Micafungin belongs to a class of drugs called echinocandins. How to Use: This medication is administered as an injection into a vein, typically once daily over one hour, as directed by your doctor. The dosage and duration of treatment depend on your medical condition and response to therapy. Before use, visually inspect the product for particles or discoloration. Infusion reactions may occur during administration. Continue using the medication for the full prescribed duration, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Possible Side Effects: Common side effects may include swelling, redness, or irritation at the injection site, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, headache, or difficulty sleeping. Remember, this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for guidance. Precautions: Before using micafungin, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, other echinocandin antifungal drugs (e.g., anidulafungin, caspofungin), or any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Some brands of this medication may contain sodium. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. It is unknown if this drug passes into breast milk. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription, non-prescription drugs, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and exhibits serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Notes: While using this medication, lab and/or medical tests (e.g., liver and kidney function, complete blood count) should be performed regularly. Keep all medical and lab appointments. Missed Dose: It is important to receive each dose of this medication as scheduled. If you miss a dose, contact your doctor or pharmacist immediately for a new dosing schedule. Storage: Consult the product instructions and your pharmacist for storage details. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Important Information: This is a summary and does not contain all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
